item.description:
### Changed - New apps are full, signed copies of the shell again (stubs on the shared runtime stay available with `CaravanCreationMode stub`). Each app is its own bundle, so notifications and camera, microphone and location prompts carry the app's own name and icon instead of "Caravan Runtime". - A web app's first notification asks macOS for that app's own notification permission, even when the site was already allowed before the app was converted. - Webapps: **Edit Address** (⌘L) opens the address in the title bar, over the window title, with the full URL selected. Deleting stops at the site's origin; Return goes there, Escape or a click elsewhere closes it. - **Advanced → Rebuild App Manifest** also repairs the Caravan Runtime, and shows its progress in a sheet. - Updates come from the public TwilightCoders/releases repository. 0.3.10 and earlier look for updates in a private repository and cannot reach them: install 0.3.12 by hand once; later versions arrive through **Check for Updates…**.
### Added - **Advanced → Convert Apps to Standalone…** and a right-click **Convert to Standalone App…** turn stub apps into full apps, keeping name, icon, bundle id, logins and settings. The stub is archived first (`~/Library/Application Support/Caravan/Backups`) and a failed conversion is undone. An app that is running converts when you quit it. `Caravan.app --convert-to-standalone "Name,Other Name"` converts named apps at launch. - Webapps keep each tab's back / forward history across relaunches, and Back / Forward are dimmed when there is nowhere to go. - Webapps open new windows where you last left one, instead of centered.
### Fixed - Find on Page (⌘F) no longer blanks the page: the find bar painted its background over everything below it, and a match the page had hidden could scroll the page away. - A page's `alert()` no longer freezes the page: the page keeps drawing behind the alert instead of going blank. - Stub apps launch again after a macOS update (error -10674): Caravan re-registers the runtime when macOS has forgotten it.
